A1.justification: Both complete PDFs describe the same DCM research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite layout changes and section renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original VBench and latency measurements, human preference results, component ablations, and supplementary experiments and generated examples.

after.justification: v2 retains these original quantitative experiments, human preference results, ablations, and supplementary results.

M1.justification: The semantic/detail experts, two-stage training, timestep-dependent layers and LoRA, expert-specific losses, and inference switching remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same VBench text-to-video evaluation, human-study material, and qualitative scenarios. The supplementary WAN2.1 evaluation and diverse generated examples were already present in v1.

E2.justification: LCM, PCM, and the original models remain the comparators in the corresponding experiments. Newly cited methods, including Truncated Consistency Models, are not added to reported comparisons.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1–4.3 retain the same model sizes, training budgets, samplers, video dimensions, evaluation metrics, and four/eight-step comparisons. The human-study protocol and supplementary expert-step allocation are also unchanged.

E4.justification: The expert-variant analysis, component ablations, kappa sensitivity sweep, and sampling-process visualizations are retained. The appendix's SVG compatibility experiment is also present in both versions.

E5.justification: Neither version reports additional repeated-run information, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The reporting of point estimates and aggregated human preferences remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 retain identical entries, including four-step DCM VBench totals of 83.83 for HunyuanVideo and 79.99 for CogVideoX. The figures and appendix retain the same qualitative findings, SVG speedup, and WAN2.1 scores.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(10), including consistency and expert-specific loss definitions, are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same claims about optimization conflict, parameter-efficient expert specialization, reduced sampling steps, and visual quality.

C2.justification: The interpretations of expert specialization, loss contributions, and the kappa transition remain unchanged. Both versions retain the limitation concerning unsatisfactory results below four steps, attributed to limited training data and iterations.

D1.justification: Learning rates, iteration counts, batch sizes, hardware, sampling details, and the stated code/model access link are unchanged. Supplementary implementation details move from Section 6 to Section 7 without substantive revision.

R1.justification: Sections 2.1–2.2 add brief coverage of video applications, sparse attention, feature caching, and Truncated Consistency Models. Ten references are added, but the central research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 removes the 'DCM:' title prefix, adds acknowledgements and several related-work sentences, and shortens an ablation passage. Supplementary sections are renumbered; most prose and the narrative sequence remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Existing figures are resized or repositioned, and Tables 1–3 move from page 8 to pages 6–7 near their discussions. The display contents and numbering are retained; supplementary figure pages render identically.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves related-work coverage through relevant truncated-consistency, sparse-attention, and caching references, while placing result tables closer to their discussion. These contextual and presentation gains are limited; the method, empirical evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations remain unchanged.
